item.description:
• Right-click a selection to see its Sum, Average, Count, Min and Max — click one to copy it. The Sum and Avg in the status bar copy when clicked, too.
  • ⌘-click to pick cells that aren’t next to each other. Totals, copy, clear and the text actions work across all of them.
  • New quick actions in the Table menu and in right-click ▸ Calculate / Text: New Column from Calculation (Price × Qty, or a column × 8% for tax), Add Totals Row, Fill Series, and text cleanup — trim spaces, change case, join or split columns.
  • ⌘D continues a pattern: 1, 2 carries on 3, 4, 5; Mon, Tue carries on Wed, Thu.
  • Drag rows by their number to reorder them, or press ⌥⌘↑ / ⌥⌘↓. Row numbers now show by default.
  • Keep Sorted Order makes a sort permanent. Sorting used to change only the view, so saving kept the original order.
  • Ctrl-click opens the menu instead of dropping your selection, big totals no longer show as 1.23457e+06, and inserting or deleting a column no longer leaves the table sorted by the wrong column.

• Close Notepad with several tabs open and they all come back where you left them — including the window arrangement. Two windows of two tabs used to return as one window of four.
  • Scratch tabs no longer ask to be saved. Closing or quitting with four untitled tabs open asked four times; now it asks nothing and simply brings them back. Named files still ask, because their changes affect a real file on disk.
  • Your tabs now survive a crash or a force-quit, not just a tidy quit. The session is saved every few seconds instead of only on the way out.
  • After an unexpected quit, Notepad no longer reopens a pile of empty windows.
  • ⌘T reliably opens a tab. It sometimes opened a separate window instead.
  • Scratch tabs you haven't touched for a couple of sessions stop reopening on their own — they move to File ▸ Reopen Closed Tab (⇧⌘T) rather than being discarded. Saved files are never aged out.

• Closing a tab no longer throws away unsaved work. ⌘W and the red close button now ask before discarding changes, the way quitting always has — previously they just closed, with no warning and nothing kept.
  • New: File ▸ Reopen Closed Tab (⇧⌘T) brings a closed tab back with its text intact, even one you closed by accident.
  • Your open tabs are now saved when a window closes, not only when you quit.
  • Quitting no longer discards your changes if you choose Save and then dismiss the save panel — it stops and waits instead.

• Files that aren't UTF-8 — a spreadsheet exported from Excel on Windows, say — now open properly instead of coming up blank. Saving keeps the file's original encoding and line endings.
  • Saving an empty document over a file that still has content now asks first.
  • Opening a file that isn't text is refused, rather than filling the window with garbage you could save over the original.
  • Printing works. ⌘P prints the document, and a CSV prints as a real table with the column headings repeated on every page.
  • Go to Line (⌘L) jumps to a line number, or to a row when a CSV is showing as a grid.
  • The grid now uses the same monospaced font as the editor, so figures line up. Columns align themselves: numbers to the right, short entries like Yes/No centred, text to the left.
  • Zoom (⌘+ and ⌘−) now works in grid view as well as the editor.
  • Undo works in the grid — cell edits, row deletions and pastes can all be taken back.
  • Insert Row and Duplicate Row added to the grid's right-click menu.
  • Replace All now works in grid view instead of quietly throwing the replacements away.

• Fixed a CSV bug where a quote or inch mark (5" pipe) merged rows and could corrupt the file on save.
  • Quitting with unsaved changes now prompts to save instead of discarding them.
  • CSV and TSV files now open from Finder, and opening a file no longer silently does nothing.
  • Launch no longer opens several blank windows.
  • Paste from Google Sheets now grows the grid instead of dropping extra rows.
  • Save As keeps the file's own extension instead of forcing .txt.
  • Restored tabs come back in the order you left them.
  • Faster typing in large JSON and other big files.

• Paste from Google Sheets now auto-switches to grid mode (5+ rows).
  • New seamless automatic updates.
  • About Notepad shows the current version.
• Testing the new Sparkle automatic update path.

• New automatic update system (Sparkle) — updates now install seamlessly.
  • Paste from Google Sheets auto-switches to grid mode.
